meta.disclaimer: Open-source situational awareness. Analytical judgements, not market-implied probabilities. Transit counts vary by source (AIS-dark vessels, differing windows). Treat as directional. Not investment, legal, or operational advice.

headline.status_line: Deal holding after weekend wobble; Hormuz de-confliction line established; commercial normalisation still weeks away
headline.strait_status: Contested-but-transiting: political reopening, NOT commercial normalisation
headline.trade_posture: Gulf-independent routing (Cape / non-Hormuz) still the prudent base case

scenarios.name: Clean implementation
scenarios.pathway: De-mining on/near 30-day schedule; nuclear talks proceed; no snapback; Lebanon de-confliction holds
scenarios.hormuz: Physically reopens mid-to-late July; commercial normalisation through Q3
scenarios.price: Brent settles $75-82; commodity war-premium bleeds out over 4-8 wks
scenarios.trade: Normalisation on track; freight & insurance ease into Q3

scenarios.name: Slow grind
scenarios.pathway: Deal holds politically but implementation drags; recurring Lebanon-triggered closure scares walked back via mediation
scenarios.hormuz: Reopens late; normalisation pushed to Q4
scenarios.trade: Berth & vessel capacity the binding constraint as flows resume unevenly

scenarios.name: Nuclear-phase breakdown / snapback
scenarios.pathway: War-end & Hormuz hold, but 60-day nuclear talks collapse; UNSC snapback reimposed
scenarios.hormuz: Stays physically open; financial/insurance plumbing re-tightens
scenarios.trade: Physical flows OK; sanctions/financial-channel risk returns to Gulf trade

scenarios.name: Ceasefire relapse
scenarios.pathway: Lebanon flare-up or IRGC spoiler breaks the deal; kinetic activity resumes; Iran enforces closure
scenarios.trade: Emergency posture; pre-positioned inventory & non-Hormuz routing critical

transit.unit: commercial vessels/day through Strait of Hormuz
transit.note: CENTCOM reports much higher counts (55 on 20 Jun) than commercial trackers (12-35). Gap = AIS-dark vessels + differing windows + political framing. Trend erratic; dipped on 21 Jun closure scare.

gates.name: Physical
gates.detail: Mines still being cleared; at least one found post-signing. De-mining coordination mechanism only agreed 22 Jun.

gates.name: Insurance (JWC)
gates.detail: No JWLA circular easing Listed Areas. War-risk premium still ~8x pre-war; 6 P&I clubs withdrew cover.

gates.name: Crew / Labour (ITF/IBF)
gates.detail: Warlike-Area status not lifted. Seafarers retain refusal + double-pay rights.

gates.name: Commercial
gates.detail: Maersk/MSC still routing via Cape of Good Hope; major carriers have not returned.

signals.label: Lebanon de-confliction cell
signals.why: Araghchi: 'first real test' of the deal

watchlist: De-mining mechanism: actual clearance activity (not just the agreement to clear)
Lebanon de-confliction cell effectiveness - the fuse most likely to break the deal
Frozen-funds sequencing dispute (Iran wants release before final talks; US rejects)
Daily transit count stabilising vs swinging - tells you if de-confliction line works
Any single vessel attack - would flip Scenario B->D

hold: Non-Hormuz / Cape routing as prudent base case until gates clear
Elevated inventory buffers on Gulf-dependent supply chains
do_now: Secure berth & vessel capacity ahead of any reopening scramble
Lock forward charters with laycan flexibility
Pre-negotiate war-risk insurance triggers with brokers
Track next Hormuz JWLA circular via war-risk broker
stand_down: Peak-crisis contingency measures as conditions de-escalate (conditionally)
